title: GIT-D evidence staleness: `badf_gate.py git-staleness` renders CURRENT / SOURCE_ADVANCED / STALE_EVIDENCE / TARGET_MOVED against a stored git-baseline record (GIT-I05, read-only) + commit-integrity subskill
objective: Make staleness a measured verdict, not a remembered rule. `badf_gate.py git-staleness <baseline-record.json> [<path>]` loads a git-baseline record (tolerating the trailing PASS line of a redirected git-baseline run), re-observes the tree through git_baseline(), and renders CURRENT (exit 0: same source head, target SHA and policy epoch), SOURCE_ADVANCED (HELD 3: source moved, recorded head is an ancestor of the new head), STALE_EVIDENCE (HELD 3: recorded head is NOT an ancestor -- amend/rebase/reset/cherry-pick -- or the policy epoch changed; carries the contract's rewrite record old_source_head / new_source_head / kind history_rewrite / old_head_still_reachable / invalidated), TARGET_MOVED (HELD 3: target changed, source unchanged); combined cases report all flags and the strictest disposition; index/worktree count deltas are informational only. Refuses BLOCKED (exit 1) a file that is not a git-baseline record and a record taken in another checkout (a baseline binds a checkout). Read-only, deterministic modulo observed_at, counts only. The commit-integrity subskill carries the nested loop's commit discipline and the rule: bind a baseline before verification, run git-staleness before publishing or opening a PR, recompute on a rewrite -- never relabel. CI stores the runner's own baseline and checks it (CURRENT) as the positive control.
business_value: The state machine lists the staleness triggers and the evidence contract defines the rewrite record, but nothing detected either: in this program's last two work packages the self-dossier was twice bound to a stale base after a rebase, caught once by compose refusing a 154 KB misbinding and once by hand. GIT-C produces the record; GIT-D consumes it, closing GIT-I05 deterministically without any mutation authority -- GTGM v0.1 sections 9, 15 and 17 (GIT-D).

acceptance_criteria: unchanged -> CURRENT/0; new commit -> SOURCE_ADVANCED/3 with an ancestor old head; amend and reset --hard -> STALE_EVIDENCE/3 with source_rewritten and both heads; rebase onto a moved target -> STALE with target_changed + merge_base_changed; target moved alone -> TARGET_MOVED/3; epoch change -> STALE with epoch_changed; a dirty tree without history change stays CURRENT
